subject: MAP: evaluation plan & cost-driver sensitivity (batching + cache)
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
To: Lydia Park <lydia@veridian.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Date: Jun 7, 2025, 09:12 AM -07:00
Subject: MAP kickoff: evaluation inputs we need (tokens/$, cache & batching assumptions)

Hi Lydia — great talking yesterday. Per our call, we'd like to formalize a short mutual action plan (MAP) and a compact evaluation run so Veridian can validate costs and SLA tradeoffs before signoff. The two things that repeatedly drive variation in unit economics are: (1) tokens-per-request assumptions (prompt + response) and (2) effective cache + batching behavior.

Ask: can you confirm the following by end of week so we can lock MAP milestones?
- Representative traffic profile (avg requests/minute, peak RPS windows) — a CSV or simple bullet list is fine.
- Typical prompt template(s) or example payloads we can token-count against.
- Any existing caching expectations (TTL, ability to cache deterministic responses, % of identical requests).
- Procurement timeline (PO/contact, target signature date).

Proposed MAP & eval skeleton (we'll fill details once we get the profile):
- Week 0: exchange traffic samples + sign MAP
- Week 1–2: two-week eval (canary in prod or dedicated test pool) with monitoring (tokens/day, P95 latency, cache hit rate)
- Cost checkpoints: daily burn + a mid-eval review with cost projection at observed cache/batch rates

I've attached a quick MAP checklist (map_checkpoint_tracker.xlsx) with fields we typically need — feel free to drop numbers directly into it. If you prefer, we can run a short simulator on Redwood's side using your traffic sample and return a tokens/$ sensitivity table.

We'll also need to know whether procurement has any special invoicing requirements (PO number format, tax ID). Marcus and Marissa are looped in to help with SOW/budget questions.

Thanks — Connor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
connor@redwood.ai

Attachments: map_checkpoint_tracker.xlsx (spreadsheet - MAP checkpoints template)

From: Lydia Park <lydia@veridian.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Veridian Health Procurement <procure@veridian.ai>
Date: Jun 7, 2025, 11:03 AM -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: evaluation inputs we need (tokens/$, cache & batching assumptions)

Connor — thanks, this is helpful. Quick answers and a couple clarifying Qs: 

1) Traffic profile: attached a small sample of anonymized request timestamps and a short description of the most common prompt templates. Peak windows are around 9–11am and 2–4pm PST; steady-state ~120 reqs/minute outside peaks.
2) Prompts: typical prompt+context averages ~140 tokens pre-response. Expected response length varies by flow (short confirmations ~60 tokens, narrative summaries ~400 tokens).
3) Caching: we can cache deterministic confirmation responses and some templated lookups. TTLs are conservative (5 minutes) but we'd be open to experimenting with shorter TTLs for the eval if it helps. We do not have an existing cache-hit baseline.

Questions: 
- When you say "batching threshold 32 requests" — how does batching affect latency? We need to understand worst-case P95 impact for user flows where sub-250ms latency is important.
- Can you simulate cost with two caching scenarios: (A) conservative TTL (300s) with 10% cache hit and (B) optimistic TTL (60s) with 25% cache hit?

I've attached our security questionnaire that procurement will want completed during the MAP (veridian_security_qs.pdf). Procurement wants a draft SOW up front if possible.

Thanks — Lydia
Sr. Product Manager | Veridian Health
lydia@veridian.ai

---
Attachments: veridian_security_qs.pdf (PDF - security/compliance questionnaire), traffic_sample.csv (referenced)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Lydia Park <lydia@veridian.ai>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Date: Jun 8, 2025, 08:18 AM -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: evaluation inputs we need (tokens/$, cache & batching assumptions)

Lydia — appreciate the quick turnaround and the sample. Short answers to your questions and the concrete plan we propose for the eval: 

1) Batching impact on latency (practical summary):
- Redwood uses dynamic batching; small batches (<=8 requests) are aggregated in <10ms; medium batches (9–32) introduce a small aggregation delay (~25–40ms) before kernel execution; large batches (>32) can push aggregation delay higher but improve tokens/$ substantially.
- For interactive flows where P95 <250ms is required, we recommend configuring a short max-wait (15–25ms) and a batch size cap of 32 to balance cost and latency.

2) Simulation plan (we'll run both scenarios you requested):
- Baseline token assumptions we will use unless you provide exact templates: prompt avg 140 tokens, response avg 220 tokens (we used a conservative response median for cost sim).
- Caching scenarios to simulate:
  A) TTL 300s, cache-hit 10%
  B) TTL 60s, cache-hit 25%
- We'll also produce a third "real-world" projection using your prompt split (confirmations vs narrative) you shared in the sample.

3) Proposed MAP/eval timeline (firm):
- Day 0: finalize MAP and sign-off (we can accept a short e-mail signoff if procurement needs time on the SOW).
- Day 1–3: provisioning and baseline run (synthetic traffic + your sample replay).
- Day 4–17: two-week live eval (we recommend a canary traffic slice ~10% of production with full telemetry).
- Day 10: mid-eval cost projection & threshold check (if observed tokens/$ > threshold we agreed, auto-escalate to price mitigation discussion).

4) Cost checkpoints & acceptance criteria (short):
- Daily token consumption report (tokens/day) + cost/day estimate
- P95 latency target for interactive flows <=250ms (can be relaxed to 350ms for non-interactive batches)
- Cache hit rate target to reach expected cost model (we'll provide a target range once sims complete)

Logistics: we can draft a short SOW and share today if that helps procurement. I'll attach a one-page MAP tracker in Drive and populate the fields we need.

Thanks — Marissa
VP, Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
